name: Tunisia
tagline: Carthage, the Sahel and the desert south
summary: Carthage on the bay of Tunis, Roman Dougga and El Jem, the Sahara at Douz and Tozeur, and a Mediterranean coast that has been in the tourism business for sixty years.

entries.caption: Carthage, the Sahel and the Desert
entries.description: Mediterranean at the top, olive plains through the middle, and the Sahara at the bottom.
entries.subject: the ruins of Carthage above the bay of Tunis

entries.caption: Coast to Chott
entries.description: The Cap Bon coast, the olive Sahel, and the salt flats of the Chott el Djerid.
entries.subject: the salt crust of the Chott el Djerid

entries.caption: Ichkeul and the Desert
entries.description: Ichkeul's wintering waterfowl, and the desert fox and gazelle of the south.
entries.subject: flamingos on the lake at Ichkeul

entries.caption: Not a Safari Country
entries.description: The wildlife here is birds and desert species, and Ichkeul is the reason to bring binoculars.
entries.subject: waders feeding on a Tunisian coastal wetland

entries.caption: The Dorsale
entries.description: The Atlas tail crosses the north — Jebel Chambi is 1,544 metres and the highest point.
entries.subject: the ridge of the Tunisian Dorsale in winter light

entries.caption: The Oasis Cascades
entries.description: Chebika, Tamerza and Mides — the mountain oases of the west, with water in a dry country.
entries.subject: the palm oasis and waterfall at Chebika

entries.caption: The Medjerda
entries.description: The only permanent river, running out of Algeria and across the northern plain.
entries.subject: the Medjerda river crossing the northern plain

entries.caption: The Mediterranean
entries.description: Hammamet, Djerba and Cap Bon — twelve hundred kilometres of it, and warm from May.
entries.subject: the whitewashed seafront at Sidi Bou Said

entries.caption: Cork Oak in the North
entries.description: The Kroumirie forest of cork oak in the north-west, which surprises everyone.
entries.subject: cork oak forest in the Kroumirie hills

entries.caption: Desert, Diving, Dunes
entries.description: Camel treks from Douz, dune camps on the erg, and diving off Tabarka.
entries.subject: camels crossing dunes on the Grand Erg oriental

entries.caption: Punic, Roman, Arab, Berber
entries.description: Four layers, all of them still visible, and often in the same town.
entries.subject: a Roman mosaic floor in a Tunisian museum

entries.caption: The Berber South
entries.description: The ksour of Tataouine, and the underground houses of Matmata.
entries.subject: an underground Berber courtyard house at Matmata

entries.caption: Couscous, Brik and Harissa
entries.description: Friday couscous, brik straight out of the pan, and harissa on everything.
entries.subject: a brik being fried at a Tunisian market stall

entries.caption: Carthage and the Sahara Festival
entries.description: The Carthage film and music festival in summer, and the Douz Sahara festival in December.
entries.subject: riders at the Sahara festival at Douz

entries.caption: Mosaic, Ceramic and Silver
entries.description: Roman mosaic technique still taught, Nabeul ceramic, and Berber silver from the south.
entries.subject: hand-painted Nabeul ceramics on a market stall

entries.caption: Carthage, Dougga, El Jem
entries.description: El Jem's amphitheatre seats thirty-five thousand and is standing almost complete.
entries.subject: the Roman amphitheatre at El Jem

entries.caption: The Medinas
entries.description: Tunis, Sousse and Kairouan — Kairouan's mosque is among the oldest in the Maghreb.
entries.subject: the great mosque of Kairouan from its courtyard

entries.caption: Tunis and Sfax
entries.description: Tunis at the head of its lake, and Sfax's walled medina working as a medina still.
entries.subject: the medina rooftops of Tunis at dusk

entries.caption: Whitewash and Blue
entries.description: Sidi Bou Said's blue and white, and the vaulted ksour of the desert south.
entries.subject: the blue doors and white walls of Sidi Bou Said

entries.caption: The Souk and the Café
entries.description: Mint tea with pine nuts, and a souk that still mostly sells to the people who live there.
entries.subject: mint tea with pine nuts at a Tunisian café

entries.caption: Two Hours from Europe
entries.description: Short flights, shallow warm sea, and resorts that have been doing families for decades.
entries.subject: a shallow beach with families on the Tunisian coast

entries.caption: Desert and Dive
entries.description: Dune trekking from Douz, quad routes on the chott, and diving at Tabarka.
entries.subject: a trekking party on the edge of the Grand Erg

entries.caption: Riad, Dar and Dune Camp
entries.description: Restored dar houses in the medinas, and desert camps beyond the last palm.
entries.subject: the courtyard of a restored dar in the Tunis medina

entries.caption: Oasis Water
entries.description: The oasis irrigation of Tozeur and Nefta, managing water in the driest place in the country.
entries.subject: traditional irrigation channels in the Tozeur oasis

entries.caption: Light on White
entries.description: Whitewash, blue, and desert light — the reason the film crews keep coming back.
entries.subject: white and blue architecture in strong Mediterranean light

entries.caption: Ksar Ouled Soltane
entries.description: Vaulted grain stores stacked four storeys high, and almost nobody there.
entries.subject: the stacked vaulted ksar at Ksar Ouled Soltane

entries.caption: Rome, and the Sahara, in One Week
entries.description: An amphitheatre on Monday and a dune camp on Thursday, in a country the size of England.
entries.subject: a desert road running south towards the Sahara
